detail.overview:
Can you build an AI solution that makes product information more complete, consistent and reliable?

Dis-Chem is one of South Africa's largest pharmacy and health retailers, with tens of thousands of products across health, baby, beauty, food and household. Every product needs an accurate, complete online record so that customers can find it, compare it and buy it with confidence. Search engines and AI shopping assistants also rely on structured, consistent product information to identify and recommend products correctly.

Today, Dis-Chem's product information is spread across several systems and is often incomplete or inconsistent. Product names may be abbreviated, descriptions may be missing, product attributes may differ between sources, and important information such as ingredients, usage instructions or warnings may not be structured correctly. Dis-Chem has developed a set of Product Content Guardrails, defining how product information should be presented, which fields are required for different product categories, and which sources can be trusted. Applying these standards manually across thousands of products is time-consuming and expensive.

Your task is to build an end-to-end AI solution that enriches, validates and standardises product catalogue records using information from multiple sources.

You will receive partially completed product records containing existing product information, structured fields and links to available product images. Some information will be intentionally removed or masked to simulate real-world gaps in Dis-Chem's catalogue. Your solution must identify and recover missing information, extract relevant product attributes, organise them into a predefined structured format and ensure that every fact is supported by an acceptable source.

The challenge is not simply to generate convincing product descriptions. Your solution must accurately extract and structure factual information while avoiding incorrect, unsupported or invented content. The best solutions will demonstrate how AI can automate product content enrichment at scale, producing records that are accurate, complete, consistent and suitable for use in a real retail environment.

Dis-Chem
With over 330 stores nationwide, Dis-Chem also provides services including health clinics, medication management, financial services and wellness solutions, making quality healthcare and everyday essentials more accessible to its customers. With an extensive product catalogue and a strong focus on customer experience, Dis-Chem continues to embrace innovation and technology to improve its retail operations and make product information more accurate, accessible and reliable.

X, bigly labs is where cutting-edge technology and customer obsession collide to reshape healthcare. As Dis-Chem’s innovation engine, we ignite brave thinking, turning audacious ideas into real-world solutions.…
detail.evaluation:
Phase 1 (13/11/26 - 14/12/26)
Phase 1 evaluates the ten product information fields listed in the data section submission_format.json. Exact wording is not required when the meaning is equivalent.

Text fields

- An LLM judge compares predictions with the reference information. The fields online_name, short_description, and long_description receive a semantic quality score. Each field is assessed for correctness, completeness, and whether it preserves the material meaning of the reference.

- The available scores are:
 | 1.00 | Correct and complete |
 | 0.75 | Mostly correct, with minor omissions or differences |
 | 0.50 | Partially correct |
 | 0.25 | Limited correct information |
 | 0.00 | Unusable or materially different |

- Equivalent wording can receive full credit. Missing or incorrect information lowers the score.Structured fields

- The LLM judge also evaluates the remaining fields, which contain lists or structured objects. It compares each non-empty value with the reference by meaning, including relevant details such as units, scope, and basis. It considers the values within the JSON structure rather than comparing the entire cell as text. The judge uses the supplied reference as the source of truth and does not consult product images or other sources.

- Each reference value can be matched once. A matched value is a true positive, or TP. A reference value without a matching prediction is a false negative, or FN. A prediction value that does not match the reference is an extra, including a new item in a list or an additional value in an object. The judge classifies each extra as a duplicate, acceptable, or unacceptable. Duplicate values and harmless, compatible details are not penalised.…
detail.data_or_tools:
This challenge uses retail product records from several product groups. The information in each record varies. Some records have detailed source text, while others have missing or masked values.

Your task is to enrich each record in Test_Masked.csv with accurate, useful product content in the ten output fields defined in ``submission_format.json``. The aim is to create clear product information that describes the exact item. This is not a request to fill every field. Every value should be supported by the supplied information or reliable evidence allowed by the content guide.

Start by confirming the product identity from its name, brand, category, descriptions, and specifications. Pay close attention to pack size, flavour, shade, weight, dimensions, and units. Similar products can differ in important ways, so do not transfer a detail from another item unless you can confirm it applies to the exact product.

Use unlabelled_data.csv to understand the catalogue and develop an approach that works across products. It has no target answers and should not be treated as a verified answer source for a test record.

Treat product identifiers as text.…
detail.eligibility:
Languages and tools: You may only use Python in building models for this challenge.
Who can compete: Open to all
This challenge is open to all.
Datasets, packages and general principles
The solution must use publicly-available, open-source packages only.
Note that to count, your submission must first pass processing. If your submission fails during the processing step, it will not be counted and not receive a score; nor will it count against your daily submission limit. If you encounter problems with your submission file, your best course of action is to ask for advice on the challenge page.
The winners will be paid via bank transfer, PayPal if payment is less than or equivalent to $100, or other international money transfer platform. International transfer fees will be deducted from the total prize amount, unless the prize money is under $500, in which case the international transfer fees will be covered by Zindi. In all cases, the winners are responsible for any other fees applied by their own bank or other institution for receiving the prize money. All taxes imposed on prizes are the sole responsibility of the winners.…

Teams allowed, up to 4 members
Team size: Max team size of 4
Code sharing: Multiple accounts, or sharing of code and information across accounts not in teams, is not allowed and will lead to disqualification.
detail.submission:
Submission Limits: 2 submissions per day, 20 submissions overall.
Public-Private Split: Zindi maintains a public leaderboard and a private leaderboard for each challenge. The Public Leaderboard includes approximately 30% of the test dataset. The private leaderboard will be revealed at the close of the challenge and contains the remaining 70% of the test set.
Code Review: Top 10 on the private leaderboard will receive an email requesting their code at the end of Phase 1. You will have 48 hours to submit your code.
You may participate in challenges as an individual or in a team of up to four people. When creating a team, the team must have a total submission count less than or equal to the maximum allowable submissions as of the formation date. A team will be allowed the maximum number of submissions for the challenge, minus the total number of submissions among team members at team formation. Prizes are transferred only to the individual players or to the team leader.
Multiple accounts per user are not permitted, and neither is collaboration or membership across multiple teams. Individuals and their submissions originating from multiple accounts will be immediately disqualified from the platform.
